description: The average transaction amount is the plain average of the stored, unsigned `amount`.

a.request: For every account that appears in `trans`, give the account id (`account_id`), the average of its transactions' `amount` exactly as stored (always non-negative, so credits and withdrawals both add positively), its number of transactions, and that number divided by the average number of transactions per account (averaged over all accounts in `trans`). Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest and keep exactly the first 10 rows, breaking any tie at the 10th place arbitrarily; do not round anything.
a.sql: SELECT account_id, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount, COUNT(*) AS txn_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT AVG(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM trans GROUP BY account_id)) AS ratio FROM trans GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY ratio DESC LIMIT 10

b.request: For every account in `trans`, show the account id, the plain average of the stored unsigned `amount` across all its transactions (credits, withdrawals, and VYBER rows alike, with no sign applied), its transaction count, and that count divided by the average number of transactions per account over all accounts in `trans`, ranked by that ratio highest first, limited to 10 rows, unrounded
b.sql: SELECT account_id, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount, COUNT(*) AS txn_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) FROM trans) AS ratio FROM trans GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY ratio DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: For every account in `trans`, show the account id, its average transaction `amount` across its credits and withdrawals, how many transactions it has, and that count divided by the average number of transactions per account over all accounts. Rank by that ratio, highest first, and keep only the first 10 rows (break any tie at the cut arbitrarily); don't round. The average transaction amount is the plain average of the stored, unsigned `amount`.
c.sql: SELECT account_id, AVG(CASE WHEN type IN ('PRIJEM','VYDAJ') THEN amount END) AS avg_amount, COUNT(*) AS txn_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) FROM trans) AS ratio FROM trans GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY ratio DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: For every account in `trans`, show the account id, its average transaction `amount` (the plain average of the stored, unsigned `amount` values, across its credits and withdrawals), the number of transactions it has, and that count divided by the average number of transactions per account over all accounts. Rank by that ratio, highest first, and keep only the first 10 rows (breaking any tie at the cut arbitrarily); don't round.
d.sql: SELECT account_id, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount, COUNT(*) AS txn_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) FROM trans) AS ratio FROM trans GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY ratio DESC LIMIT 10
